# Filmorax

> Filmorax is a cinematic and advertising production studio based in Agouza, Giza, Egypt. It produces commercials, corporate and brand films, cinematic social content, product videos, event coverage and full post-production for brands in Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf — from brief and treatment through the shoot day to final delivery in every platform format, with deliverables and usage rights written before filming.

## Production formats

- Commercials: 15–60 second commercials for TV and digital platforms, built around a single message — treatment and script, casting, direction, cinematography, and a master plus cut-downs for every platform.
- Corporate & Brand Films: short films that tell the company's or the brand's story visually, for launches, company pages and official occasions — screening version plus short social cuts.
- Product Videos: the product as the hero of the frame — detailed product photography and lighting, real usage footage in context, and short versions for stores and ads.
- Event Coverage: multi-camera filming of openings, launches and conferences, fast cuts for publishing during the event, and a complete aftermovie.
- Cinematic Social Content: reels and short videos with film-grade lighting and grading at social platforms' rhythm and sizes, delivered as scheduled campaign batches.
- Post-Production: editing, colour grading and correction, sound design and mixing, licensed music, motion graphics, subtitling and localisation — for footage shot by the studio or material the client already has.

## How production runs (4 stages)

1. Brief & treatment — the objective becomes a production document: one message, defined placements, and a treatment and script the client approves first.
2. Pre-production — casting, locations, crew, equipment and the shoot-day schedule, all locked on paper before the camera moves.
3. The shoot day — direction, photography, lighting and sound under schedule management, with a call sheet and double backup of all footage at wrap.
4. Post & delivery — editing, grading, sound and review rounds, then organised delivery: master, platform versions and licence files.

## Guides (free, on the landing pages)

Published on the homepages (Arabic: https://filmorax.com/#guides · English: https://filmorax.com/en.html#guides) — practical know-how from how production actually runs:

- The production brief: the document everything is built on (https://filmorax.com/en.html#guides): a shoot day is priced, cast and scheduled from the brief. It needs one objective and one message, final placements decided first (they set formats and durations), a written deliverables list (durations, versions, languages — not assumptions), and a declared approval chain for treatment, casting and final cut. Every missing answer becomes an expensive decision taken on the shoot day.
- One full shoot day: a temporary factory running 12 hours (https://filmorax.com/en.html#guides): setup, lighting and rehearsal come before the first shot; the schedule is ordered by location and daylight, not script order; a full crew works under a call sheet where overtime is a decision, not a drift; and at wrap you hold raw material backed up twice — the film itself is built in post.
- Usage rights: the film is one thing, the faces in it are another (https://filmorax.com/en.html#guides): paying for production is not owning every use forever. Talent image and voice rights are licensed separately from the edited film — by media (TV, digital/social, out-of-home, in-store, cinema), territory, duration and category exclusivity; library music and stock carry their own licence terms. Usage is written before casting, because renegotiating after a successful campaign costs far more.
- Video production for the Arab market — a guide for Turkish brands (Türkçe) (https://filmorax.com/tr.html): how a Turkish brand enters the Arab market with video — the Gulf dialect as the language of recommendation, cultural context, remote production from Cairo with filming in Egypt and Saudi Arabia, usage rights written before filming, and measurement per city and creator. Published 2026-11-07.
- UGC and influencer content with Arab creators — a second guide for Turkish brands (Türkçe) (https://filmorax.com/tr-ugc.html): why a brand film is not enough, creator selection by category and dialect before follower counts, briefing in Turkish turned into an Arabic production document with written approval, whitelisting and usage rights fixed before filming, and measurement per creator. Published 2026-11-07.
- Real production materials on the homepages (https://filmorax.com/#works): four media-production works from influUGC's own library — MUHRA, MUHRA 2, Calve and Calve 57 — as playable videos with posters. English: https://filmorax.com/en.html#works
